I have just arrived to the craziest city on earth and you probably never even heard about it.
This is Chongqing, China where they have petrol stations on top of roofs, trains that run through residential buildings, buses in the sky, elevators for cars, multi-storey restaurants floating on the river and, well, also, the deepest subway in the world.
It goes down 118 meters, which is roughly the height of a 39 storey building, and it took me 15 minutes just to get to the bottom.
But the craziest part, we're still on the ground floor.
You see, the reason people call Chongqing the 5D city is because it served as China's World War II capital.
All of those old, underground bomb shelters have since been transformed into roads, basements, and buildings.
So, good luck finding your way around.
Here, you think I'm on the ground floor, right?
Wrong.
Because if you go to one side, you'll see you're on level one.
And if you go to the other side of the square, you're now on level 18, and almost everywhere in the city is like this.
Here, we're on the 14th floor, and the elevator even shows you that.
But, if you walk outside, you're now on the ground floor again.
And if you think simply walking around the city is confusing, try driving.
One wrong turn on these roads, and you're cooked.
You might even find yourself accidentally entering the garage that is 500 meters to the bottom.
Yes, I'm still driving down as I post this video.

videos.title: This 20-year-old student spent 7 months single-handedly cleaning up a polluted river in India, and the...
videos.creator: Dylan Page
videos.transcript:
This 20-year-old student spent 7 months single-handedly cleaning up a polluted river in India, and the before and after images are so staggering people believe this is AI.
This is Bitu Tabahi.
And back in January, he became tired of waiting for the government to clean up the Ajnora river.
So he decided fine, I'll do it myself.
And let me tell you, bro went through hell.
You see, Bitu had zero financial support, meaning he had to start doing this without any safety gear, cleaning up trash with his bare hands, which unsurprisingly caused multiple infections on his skin.
But on top of that, Bitu had to dodge snakes.
He had to be careful not to fall in the river because he couldn't even swim.
And to make it even worse, instead of locals seeing this and helping him, many actually made fun of him and told him to come clean up their drains instead.
But, despite all of that, Bitu, he just kept on pushing, slowly transforming this riverbed, piece by piece.
And at one point, he was even moving 10 kg of trash every single day, and eventually, as the months went by, people started to take notice.
And today, families and visitors are returning to this riverbed for the first time in years.
The world needs more people like Bitu.
videos.caption: This is actually wild!🤯🤯 @bittu_tabahi

videos.title: The disaster in Nepal is so much worse than we could have imagined.
videos.creator: Dylan Page
videos.transcript:
The disaster in Nepal is so much worse than we could have imagined.
That thing you are seeing being swept along by the currents, that is a giant boulder the size of a building.
Anything that was in its path was swept away like it was nothing, including the dam itself, and videos captured from the mountains show the staggering scale and power of these floods.
These are literally scenes that you would see in an end of the world Hollywood movie.
More than 1,300 people are now missing, more than 20 bridges, and 40 km of road were destroyed.
Around a dozen expensive hydroelectric projects were damaged, countless trucks and vehicles were washed away, and thousands of people have been left stranded in the mountains looking at their homes in ruins.
And what a lot of people forget is that in disasters like this, it's not only humans that suffer.
I mean here we see a video of some baby elephants, which barely survived after they were also swept away.
More than 5,000 army and police rescue personnel have joined the effort, and every available aircraft in Nepal has been called in to assist, including 14 helicopters.
But, just to make matters even worse, experts are now warning of a secondary potential flooding event as a result of all the debris that was washed into the river systems from the first.
So whatever you do, keep Nepal in your thoughts and prayers.
videos.caption: Keep Nepal in your thoughts and prayers 💔

Wild.

videos.title: If you ever feel like you're being followed in Japan, visit one of these stores, because it might just...
videos.creator: Dylan Page
videos.transcript:
If you ever feel like you're being followed in Japan, visit one of these stores, because it might just save your life.
You see, in the early 2000s, Japan witnessed a concerning rise in violent crime.
And after a number of high-profile cases involving women being stalked and children attacked on the way to school, Japanese authorities tried something crazy.
They realized that these convenience stores are everywhere here, and they often even outnumber police stations and boxes.
They're also bright, full of cameras, open 24/7, and they always have at least one member of staff on duty.
So, in 2005, they launched an official nationwide crime prevention partnership with these stores.
From that day on, they would act as a safe station for women, children, or anyone who feels like they're in danger.
And in just one year after launching, the results were staggering.
More than 13,000 women took refuge in a convenience store.
Around 6,000 lost children found help here, and about 12,000 elderly people were reunited with loved ones after wandering away from home.
And now, over a decade later, more than 50,000 stores participate as safety stations, including 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, Lawson, and that covers a staggering 99% of stores nationwide.
So, make sure to share this video with someone visiting Japan, because who knows, it might just save their life.
videos.caption: Convenience stores in Japan are so much more than just stores!🤯🇯🇵
